Add traces to a figure

Source: R/basefigure.R
add_traces.Rd

add_trace() adds one trace and add_traces() several. add_trace() is an S3 generic, so packages can add methods for their own figure classes (the plotly package does for plot_ly() objects).

Usage

add_trace(fig, ...)

# S3 method for class 'go_figure'
add_trace(
  fig,
  trace,
  row = NULL,
  col = NULL,
  secondary_y = NULL,
  exclude_empty_subplots = FALSE,
  ...
)

add_traces(
  fig,
  data,
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  secondary_ys = NULL,
  exclude_empty_subplots = FALSE
)

Arguments

fig

A go_figure object.

...

Unused.

trace

A trace: a graph object such as go_scatter(), or a named list with a type element (default "scatter").

row, col

Subplot grid cell for the trace (figures created with make_subplots() only). Either may be "all" or a vector, to add the trace to several cells.

secondary_y

If TRUE, use the secondary y axis of the subplot (see the specs argument of make_subplots()).

exclude_empty_subplots

If TRUE, don't add the trace to subplots that have no traces or layout objects yet.

data

A list of traces.

rows, cols, secondary_ys

Per-trace grid cells and secondary y flags for add_traces(); a single value applies to every trace.

Value

The modified figure.

See also

The generated add_<trace type>() functions, e.g. add_scatter().

Examples

go_figure() |>
  add_trace(go_scatter(x = 1:3, y = 1:3)) |>
  add_traces(list(list(type = "scatter", y = 3:1), go_scatter(y = c(2, 2, 2))))

make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = 2) |>
  add_trace(go_scatter(y = 1:3), row = 1, col = 2)
